`scan --inline-rules` built its rule collection with an empty registry,
so a rule referencing a global util (`matches: hook`) failed to parse
with `Rule hook is not defined` in every config form. The same rule
under `ruleDirs` loaded fine: utils were only registered while walking
the project's rule directories, which inline rules never do. `scan
--stdin --inline-rules` was broken the same way (issue #2927).

Load the project's utils once (`ProjectConfig::find_utils`, reusing the
existing loader) and pass them to `from_yaml_string` in both inline
paths. No project config still falls back to no globals, and a malformed
config keeps erroring before the scan, as before.

The test drives both forms (file scan with --config and --stdin with
upward discovery) with a util-backed inline rule; without the fix it
fails with `Rule hook is not defined`.

* fix(scan): load project utils for rule files

fix(scan): bind utilDirs utils for --inline-rules and --rules (#2943)

* fix(scan): bind utilDirs utils for inline rules

`scan --inline-rules` built its rule collection with an empty registry,
so a rule referencing a global util (`matches: hook`) failed to parse
with `Rule hook is not defined` in every config form. The same rule
under `ruleDirs` loaded fine: utils were only registered while walking
the project's rule directories, which inline rules never do. `scan
--stdin --inline-rules` was broken the same way (issue #2927).

Load the project's utils once (`ProjectConfig::find_utils`, reusing the
existing loader) and pass them to `from_yaml_string` in both inline
paths. No project config still falls back to no globals, and a malformed
config keeps erroring before the scan, as before.

The test drives both forms (file scan with --config and --stdin with
upward discovery) with a util-backed inline rule; without the fix it
fails with `Rule hook is not defined`.

* fix(scan): load project utils for rule files
